archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (pitching-first)
archetype.definition: Boston built a top-three run prevention unit and a 50-28 finish after June, then was shut down in two Wild Card games because a below-average offense had nothing left.

report.headline: Elite pitching and defense, a quiet lineup, and a short October

recap.finish: 87-75, third in the AL East; lost the Wild Card Series 0-2 to NYY
recap.body:
This was a run prevention team. Boston ranked 3rd in runs allowed per game, 3rd in ERA at 3.54 and 4th in Fielding Runs at 24.8, with A grades for both the rotation and the bullpen. The offense ranked 23rd in runs per game with a .717 OPS. In a park that plays at 106 for hitters, the Red Sox scored about 4.25 runs a game and allowed about 3.77, and that margin of +0.48 per game ranked 7th in the league.

The season split into two halves. Boston was below .500 in every month through June and stood 37-47 at the turn. July changed it: 21-4, a 15-game winning streak, and only 74 runs allowed in 25 games. August added a 17-12 month built on the best run production of the year, 155 runs. From July 1 on the club went 50-28. September cooled to 12-12, and the offense was the reason: 71 runs in 24 games, under three a game. The last ten games produced 21 runs, with 1-0, 0-1 and 2-3 results against Cleveland.

The pitching staff had real depth. Payton Tolle led the rotation with 4.1 WAR, a 28.4% K% and an ERA (3.03) that matched his FIP (3.04). Ranger Suarez (3.22 ERA, 3.16 FIP) was just as solid. Sonny Gray's 2.72 ERA was the best on the staff, but his 3.47 FIP says some of it was soft contact and sequencing. At the back of the bullpen, Garrett Whitlock (1.72 ERA, 26 holds) handed games to Aroldis Chapman (35 saves, 33.3% K%). On offense, Willson Contreras was the only true middle-of-the-order bat at 151 wRC+. Ceddanne Rafaela's 4.1 WAR came from defense as much as his bat, with 11.5 Def Runs in the outfield.

The weak spots were specific. Jarren Duran took 608 plate appearances with a 69 wRC+ and a .266 OBP. Andruw Monasterio played 107 games at shortstop at an 83 wRC+ and -11.2 Def Runs, worth -0.6 WAR. Curtis Mead hit at a 133 wRC+ but got only 329 PA. Those holes help explain why a lineup graded B+ player by player still scored like a bottom-ten offense. W vs Run Diff of -2.9 also cost the Sox about three wins, roughly the gap to a 90-win season. That is the second straight year near -3.

The postseason confirmed the September slide. New York won 9-0 and 9-2, and Boston was outscored 18-2 with a .409 OPS. Contreras homered and posted a 252 wRC+; almost no one else hit. Tolle and Gray kept both games within reach early, with 4.2 innings each. The bullpen then gave up big innings, including Whitlock's 20.25 ERA in 1.1 innings.

highlights.title: Run prevention jumped to elite
highlights.body: Boston finished 3rd in runs allowed per game. Before last year's 10th, this franchise sat between 18th and 25th in that rank. The improvement is broad: four starters with ERAs at 3.65 or better and FIPs that support them, plus the 4th-best Fielding Runs total. Because both FIP and fielding back it up, this looks repeatable rather than lucky.

highlights.title: July's 21-4 rescued the season
highlights.body: The club came out of June ten games under .500, then won 21 of 25 in July, including a 15-game winning streak. The pitching drove it: 74 runs allowed in 25 games, about three per game. Without that month, this is a non-playoff season.

highlights.title: Whitlock and Chapman locked down late innings
highlights.body: Whitlock (1.72 ERA, 2.11 FIP, 26 holds) and Chapman (1.92 ERA, 35 saves) gave the bullpen a dominant final pair. Their strikeout rates, 29.8% and 33.3%, back up the results. Chapman's 10.8% BB% is the one thing worth watching.

lowlights.title: Offense fell to bottom-ten
lowlights.body: An offense ranked 23rd in runs per game is the lowest this club has produced in six seasons; it ranked between 5th and 11th from 2021 through 2025. Contreras carried the lineup almost alone. Duran's 69 wRC+ over 608 PA was a large hole near the top of the playing-time list. September's 71 runs in 24 games showed how thin the margin was.

lowlights.title: Shortstop was a two-way liability
lowlights.body: Monasterio played below average at the plate (83 wRC+) and in the field (-11.2 Def Runs), finishing at -0.6 WAR. On a team built around defense, that was the most costly regular. Trevor Story started at short in the postseason.

lowlights.title: Outclassed in the Wild Card
lowlights.body: Two road losses by a combined 18-2 ended the season. The offense posted a .409 OPS and the staff a 10.13 ERA, last among postseason teams. Two games is a tiny sample, but the lack of hitting matched how the regular season ended.

arc.note: Boston was 37-47 through June, went 21-4 in July and 50-28 the rest of the way, then played .500 in September as the offense dried up. The season ended with two blowout losses in New York.

recap.nextYear: The pitching core carries over. Tolle, Suarez and Bennett all had FIPs at or below 3.51, Gray's 2.72 ERA may drift toward his 3.47 FIP, and Sandoval's 5.12 ERA against a 3.77 FIP points to bad luck that should ease. Whitlock and Chapman give the bullpen a strong back end, though Bello's 4.33 ERA over 116.1 innings and Morán's 12.1% BB% are the soft spots. The real work is the lineup. Contreras, Rafaela, Abreu, Durbin and Rutschman form a solid core, but center-of-the-field bats like Duran's (69 wRC+) and the shortstop job (-0.6 WAR) need fixing, and Mead's 133 wRC+ argues for giving him more than 329 PA. W vs Run Diff ran about -3 in each of the last two seasons; that tends to even out, so a similar run differential should be worth roughly 90 wins. That is still short of TB's 98-win pace without a better offense.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the postseason verdict rests on just two games.
